headline: US UN envoy Mike Waltz says Washington is prepared for year-long standoff with Iran
dek: (1) The US-Iran war, which Trump initially said would last 'four to five weeks', could still be underway 12 months from now — Waltz declined to rule out another year of fighting. (2) Washington will not consider its objectives met until Iran disposes of its highly enriched nuclear material AND…
sources: Financial Times (interview with US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz)
fault_line: 'This war has ended 17 times already — another year?' vs 'hold the line until enrichment is dead'; secondary line: sanctions/pump-price pain on civilians vs maximum pressure on the regime

sections.what_happened: (1) The US-Iran war, which Trump initially said would last 'four to five weeks', could still be underway 12 months from now — Waltz declined to rule out another year of fighting. (2) Washington will not consider its objectives met until Iran disposes of its highly enriched nuclear material AND accepts a 'meaningful agreement on their domestic enrichment'. (3) 'The president and the US Navy can maintain this blockade [on Iranian ports] for the foreseeable future'; the administration is still 'tightening' its economic pressure campaign.
sections.what_verified: CBS News (Oct 23); Financial Times' own verified Facebook post; thecompositeeye.ca (published 2026-10-23T02:54:45-04:00); hathalyoum.net (2026-10-23T12:34+03:00); turkiyetoday.com; streamlinefeed.co.ke — all attribute the same quotes to the FT interview. sections.what_disputed: Iranian position unchanged: NSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei — no negotiations / no Hormuz reopening until Iran's seven conditions are met. Araghchi disputed Waltz's framing of the rejected uranium offer (civicintelligence.news). Trump claims more oil passes through Hormuz now than before the conflict — undercutting the blockade narrative.
sections.why_matters: The war the president said would last 'four to five weeks' may last a year — the envoy names the price of ending it: no enriched uranium, no domestic enrichment deal, no deal. Connect: 100-day blockade ($25B denied) + $114 oil + post-midterm strike plans. Dot-connecting monologue, pocketbook first.
